newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs designate pioneers of future stock market.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs designate pioneers of future stock market.

text.p: Kazakhstan has selected the pioneer companies to be listed on its new stock market, a National Securities Commission official said on Monday.

"The government has approved two lists of companies," Commission Deputy Chairman Galina Shalgimbayeva told Reuters at the weekend. "We believe the first deals will take place by the end of August or the beginning of September," she said.
State-owned shares of nine companies on the first list will be sold directly on the exchange, she said, but gave no details.
Companies in the second list of four firms will be sold to portfolio investors with the help of foreign investment banks, she said.
Kazakhstan has already privatised large, even controlling stakes, to strategic investors in recent tenders that are part of the government's rapid privatisation scheme for key industries.
Last December the government approved a list of some 60 big local companies designated to form a system of Kazakh "blue chip" and become the core of the stock market.

Officials in the resource-rich Central Asian country five times the size of France and with a population of just 16.7 million people say foreign portfolio investment is crucial to the success of the shares market.

The new list of stakes to be sold directly on the market include three percent of AO Alyuminii Kazakhstana alumina works, two percent of AO Kazkhrom chrome producer, 30 percent of miner AO Yuzhno-Toparskoye Rudoupravleniye, 4.5 percent of titanium magnesium producer AO Ust-Kamenogorsky Titano-Magniyevy Kombinat, 39 percent of lead producer AO Shymkentsky Svintsovy Zavod and 10 percent of Halyk Savings Bank.
Shalgimbayeva said large foreign investment institutions would have to attract portfolio investors for the second group.
"Foreign investors will work with Kazakh brokers through investment banks," she said. "The banks' interest is their commission fee."

The second list includes a five-percent stakes in Zhezkazgantsvetmet copper producer and Mangistaumunaigaz and Aktobemunaigaz oil companies. Investors will also be offered a 4.5-percent stake in the Kazakhtelekom telecoms monopoly.
Kazakhstan has already begun the process of selecting foreign banks to work with each of the four companies.

Shalgimbayeva said the final round of the tender would be held on June 30 among eight finalists including ABN AMRO Bank, Salomon Brothers and Global Securities, Daiwa, HSBC, UBS, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, a consortium of Malaysian broker companies and the Kazakh International Bank.
